name: pay-first-won
about: One concept clearly did well over many leads and one spent for nothing.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook pay_first (pay first) and scene equipment_on_road (truck on the road) spent $612.40 in the last 28 days over 48210 impressions and brought 31 leads, $19.75 per lead.
Our ads with hook life_first (life first) and scene home_street (home street) spent $188.00 in the last 28 days over 15120 impressions and brought no lead.
Of 31 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 29 were called and 22 were reached.

output.audience: Class A drivers who meet the experience requirement and run flatbed, or want to, on Midwest lanes. Many likely get home less often now or drive for a large fleet. A plain pay per mile, home weekly and an assigned truck would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, over a loaded flatbed running a Midwest highway.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile, and the work is flatbed on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: This hook and scene brought a fair number of leads at a cost per lead well under the benchmark's pause level. It is the best-measured pairing we have, so keep it running.

angles.idea: Say plainly who the job is for: Class A, the experience requirement, flatbed work, Midwest lanes.
angles.proof: The opening is Class A regional flatbed on Midwest lanes and states an experience requirement.
angles.why: The lead outcomes show how many leads were reached but not who qualified. Stating the requirement and the lanes up front screens before a recruiter calls. Untested here.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck, seen from the driver's seat with the flatbed in the mirror.
angles.proof: The opening comes with an assigned truck and the work is flatbed.
angles.why: An assigned truck is a concrete fact that experienced drivers weigh. No earlier ad of ours led with equipment, so nothing has been measured for this hook.

angles.idea: Lead with home weekly, shown as the truck parked with the week's work done.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly on regional lanes.
angles.why: Life first on a home street spent past the benchmark's no-lead pause level and brought nothing. Home weekly is still a core fact, so try it with the truck in frame rather than drop it.

angles.idea: Lead with the small fleet where dispatch knows your name, backed by the terms listed plainly.
angles.proof: The carrier describes itself as a small fleet where dispatch knows your name, and offers an assigned truck and a retirement plan.
angles.why: The fleet's own description sets it apart from large carriers, and the listed terms give it substance. No earlier ad used a proof hook, so this is a test.
